verses.text: So now there’s no condemnation for people who belong to Christ Jesus and walk by the Spirit, not by the flesh. None, fam.
The Spirit’s law of life in Christ Jesus has broken sin and death’s hold on me.
The Law couldn’t pull it off because human weakness got in the way. God did: he sent his own Son in human likeness, as a sin offering, and condemned sin in human flesh.
He did this so the Law’s right requirement could be fulfilled in us, as we walk by the Spirit, not by the flesh.
People led by the flesh set their minds on fleshly things; people led by the Spirit focus on what the Spirit wants.
A mind fixed on the flesh heads toward death. A mind led by the Spirit brings life and peace.
The flesh-focused mind is at odds with God. It won’t submit to God’s Law—in fact, it can’t.
People living by the flesh can’t please God.
But you’re not living by the flesh; you’re living by the Spirit—if God’s Spirit really lives in you. Anyone without Christ’s Spirit doesn’t belong to him.
If Christ is in you, your body is dead because of sin, but your spirit is alive because of righteousness.
If the Spirit of the God who raised Jesus from the dead lives in you, then the God who raised Christ Jesus will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit living in you.
So then, family, we owe the flesh nothing. We don’t have to live by its demands.
If you live by the flesh, you’ll die. But if by the Spirit you put the body’s sinful actions to death, you’ll live.
Everyone led by God’s Spirit is a child of God.
You didn’t get a spirit that drags you back into slavery and fear. You received the Spirit who adopts you, and by him we cry, “Abba! Father!”
The Spirit himself confirms to our spirit that we are God’s children.
And if we’re children, we’re heirs too—heirs of God and coheirs with Christ, if we suffer with him so we can also share his glory.
I’m convinced the suffering we face now can’t even compare with the glory God is about to reveal in us.
All creation is on tiptoe, waiting for God’s children to be revealed.
Creation was subjected to frustration—not by its own choice, but by the one who subjected it—with hope
that creation itself will be freed from decay’s slavery and share in the glorious freedom of God’s children.
We know the whole creation has been groaning and going through labor pains together right up to now.
And it’s not just creation. We have the Spirit’s firstfruits, and we groan inside too as we wait for adoption to be complete and our bodies to be redeemed.
We were saved in hope. But if you can already see what you hope for, that’s not hope—who hopes for what they already see?
But if we hope for what we can’t see yet, we wait for it with patience.
The Spirit helps us in our weakness. We don’t even know how to pray as we should, but the Spirit himself pleads for us with groans too deep for words.
God, who searches hearts, knows what the Spirit means, because the Spirit pleads for God’s people in line with God’s will.
We know God works all things together for good for those who love him, who are called according to his purpose.
Those God knew beforehand, he also marked out to become like his Son, so the Son would be the firstborn among many brothers and sisters.
Those he marked out, he also called; those he called, he also made right; those he made right, he also brought into glory.
So what do we say to all this? If God is for us, who can stand against us?
God didn’t hold back his own Son but handed him over for all of us. Won’t he also freely give us everything with him?
Who can bring a charge against God’s chosen people? God is the one who makes them right.
Who can condemn us? Christ Jesus died—and more than that, he was raised. He’s at God’s right hand, and he’s pleading for us.
What can separate us from Christ’s love? Trouble, distress, persecution, hunger, having no clothes, danger, or violence?
Scripture says, “For your sake we face death all day long; we’re treated like sheep lined up for slaughter.”
No! Through the one who loved us, we come through all of this more than conquerors. 💪
I’m convinced nothing can separate us—not death or life, angels or rulers, what’s happening now or what’s coming, any power,
nothing above us or below us, nothing else in all creation can separate us from God’s love in Christ Jesus our Lord. ❤️
